title: The Levelled Disc
logline: A clay-worker makes and re-makes a plain disc for a meditation teacher, smoothing it flat again every time it dries and cracks, so that someone else will have something completely uninteresting to look at.
human_question: What can a person do with attention that has nowhere interesting to land?

situation.what_happens: A clay-worker takes an order for training discs from a teacher who runs meditation classes: sourcing clay of the right colour, picking out grit and stones, levelling the surface until it is as even as a drum skin, and levelling it again each time it dries and cracks. The order is small, the object is deliberately plain, and the work is repetitive to the point of monotony. At the end the discs are wrapped and delivered, and the maker's involvement ends.
situation.who_is_involved: A clay-worker and their household, who do this alongside ordinary domestic ware; the teacher who ordered the discs; the people who will use them, who are strangers to the maker.
situation.what_is_at_stake: For the maker, a small paid order and their reputation for getting a surface truly flat. For the film, the risk of turning a livelihood into a metaphor, or implying the maker practises what the discs are for.
situation.how_it_unfolds: Clay work moves at the speed of drying: shape, wait, crack, repair, wait. The pressures are weather, fuel and a delivery date. It ends when the order is delivered, or when the clay or the weather defeats the deadline. Whether the maker has any interest in what the object is used for is for them to say, not for the film to arrange.

concept_merge.why_together: C087 (kasina meditation) contributes the object itself: the sources describe preparing a disc of smooth reddish clay, levelling it until it is like a drum face, and attending to it by name rather than by its colour or feel [C087-P4:L209–L213]. C085 (the compendium of meditation subjects) contributes the fact that this is only one of forty things attention can be given, chosen to fit the person [C085-P:L47]. C013 (the fine-material minds) contributes the sources' image of what such long looking is for: bringing an object close and looking at it until it is completely clear [C013-P:L48–L52].
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: Together they show that the discipline of stillness begins in ordinary craft, with an object made dull on purpose, and that the object matters far less than the choosing and the attending. The making alone would be a craft film; the list alone would be a lecture.

concept_links.why: The digest describes exactly this act of craft: picking out pebbles and twigs, kneading and levelling the clay, and levelling it again when it cracks, until the surface is as smooth as a drum skin [C087-P4:L209–L213]. The digest also warns that the powers the source lists as fruits of kasina practice must never be presented as verified fact or as a promise [C087-P4:L464–L484].

The digest lists the disc first among forty subjects, and insists the choice is matched to the person and given by a teacher [C085-P:L47]. The film can show one object being made without itemising the list.

The Pradeepika's image for deep concentration is someone who brings an object close, stops looking elsewhere and looks long at its colours and marks until it is completely clear [C013-P:L48–L52]. The finished disc is what such attention is meant to rest on; the film makes no claim that the maker practises.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: The training the texts describe can start with something a person makes by hand and deliberately keeps uninteresting, and the care goes into the making, not into the object being worth looking at.
what_must_be_real: The clay-worker's actual livelihood, actual order and actual relationship with whoever buys the discs. The maker is never shown as practising, and no one is presented as having attained anything.
position_hint: opening candidate if kept separately: an ordinary way Object 10 could be acquired, since the group's opening asks for something that helps stillness.
risks: Turning craft into pure metaphor with no livelihood at stake
Implying the maker practises kasina, or that the object confers anything
Letting the traditional fruits of the practice be heard as a promise
drop_if: No clay-worker can be found who genuinely supplies such objects to a willing teacher
The only way to film it would be to commission an order that would not otherwise exist

connections.note: Its situation detail, the plain object made and re-levelled by hand, now sits inside the class film.

selection.reason: Its object and its craft detail strengthen the C087 link inside IDEA-0176, which has the episode slot.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
